Civil and Federal Government Satcom Programmes, Tenders and RFP Portals to Track: Europe and Asia-Pacific (with notable programmes elsewhere)

GovernmentEuropeLEO Satellite

A companion to the defence-focused tenders report, covering civil and federal government satcom programmes, tenders and official procurement portals as of November 13, 2026. It focuses on emergency services and blue-light networks, civil protection, digital resilience, public warning, maritime and aviation safety, border and coastguard, and rural or universal-service connectivity. Section 1 lists 95 official civil portals (EU, national European, Asia-Pacific, plus other regions and multilateral, each curl-checked), with Europe and Asia-Pacific programmes in depth and shorter notes on the US, Canada, Brazil, Saudi Arabia and Kenya (South Africa appears as a portal). Near-term closings include BEREC Office crisis-communication devices (Nov 19, 2026), Lithuania State Border Guard satcom (Dec 3) and an Estonian Starlink framework (Dec 14). The EU’s proposed EUCCS would use IRIS² and GOVSATCOM as back-up for first responders from 2030.

Civil and Federal Government Satcom Programmes, Tenders and RFP Portals to Track: Europe and Asia-Pacific (with notable programmes elsewhere)

Emergency services and blue-light networks, civil protection and disaster response, digital resilience and critical-infrastructure back-up, public warning and direct-to-device, maritime/aviation safety, border and coastguard, universal service and rural connectivity | Status as of November 13, 2026 | Companion to the defence-focused report of Nov 12, 2026

Prepared for Paul. Citations in square brackets are clickable and map to the numbered References. Portal links in Section 1 and the watchlist are clickable directly. Status labels: OPEN · RFI / MARKET ENGAGEMENT · PENDING AWARD · AWARDED · PLANNED · Items marked [UNVERIFIED] come only from press, analyst or aggregator sources with no official confirmation found. Items marked “inference” are my reading of official dates, not a published plan. Deadlines are as published by the buyer, in the buyer’s local time zone.

Executive summary

  • Civil satcom demand is now driven by mission-critical broadband migrations, not by stand-alone satellite programmes. Every large European blue-light network is moving from TETRA to 3GPP broadband on commercial mobile networks, and each one is writing satellite in as back-up or gap-fill rather than buying a dedicated constellation: the UK’s ESN (voice service ready targeted March 2028, mass transition from Q4 2028) [22], France’s RRF (national roll-out decided Sep 1, 2026) [28], Sweden’s SWEN/Rakel G2 [48], Norway’s new Nødnett [42], Finland’s Virve 2 [50] and the Dutch C2000 successor VMX [37]. The procurement opportunities are therefore satellite backhaul for deployable cells, LEO back-up for priority sites, air-to-ground and maritime coverage lots, and D2D gap-fill, usually as sub-lots or follow-on buys.
  • The EU has put satellite into law for first responders. On Sep 30, 2026 the Commission proposed the EU Critical Communication System (EUCCS), linking 31 national networks, with EU satellites as back-up during blackouts and connection of Member States starting in 2030 [1]. The proposal estimates €3.571bn of public investment and requires EUCCS users to use GOVSATCOM and IRIS² services, including direct-to-device, when terrestrial networks fail [2]. GOVSATCOM itself has been operational since January 2026 for civil protection, border and maritime users [4], and the August 2026 IRIS² agreement adds 66 satellites “for defence, security, and emergency services” [5].
  • Open or closing now (civil buyers): BEREC Office crisis-communication satellite devices (BEREC/2026/OP/0006, Nov 19, 2026) [7]; Lithuania State Border Guard satcom equipment and access (TED 742977-2026, Dec 3, 2026) [13]; Estonia’s Riigiside Sihtasutus Starlink service framework (TED 791815-2026, 36 months, €600k estimate, €1M cap, Dec 14, 2026) [12]; and the ESA ARTES 4S announcement for maritime safety and critical communications (open until at least November 2026, rolling) [9]. Recently closed and in evaluation: TenneT’s €3.6M crisis satcom framework [19], Kenya’s Digital Health Agency LEO framework (closed Nov 2, 2026) [84], and the Philippines’ PIALEOS LEO rebid (closed Sep 9, 2026) [70].
  • Asia-Pacific is subsidy- and obligation-led. Japan’s J-LEO grant was decided for RAST with Rakuten Mobile [53,54], and MIC’s FY2027 request includes ¥10.0bn for mobile base-station resilience using batteries, generators, solar and satellite [60]. Australia’s Universal Outdoor Mobile Obligation became law in October 2026 with a default start of Dec 31, 2027, which the Minister can push back to end-2030 [72]. Korea is studying a sovereign LEO network by 2035 (128–512 satellites, about KRW 4–14 trillion) [62]. Taiwan’s moda maintains 196 OneWeb/SES back-up sites under a NT$400M common-supply contract that runs to Dec 31, 2026 [64,65].
  • Watch for in 2027: a Taiwan follow-on contract for the government non-GEO back-up network (current contract ends Dec 31, 2026; inference) [65]; a re-tender of Italy’s Civil Protection emergency satellite connectivity service (24-month contract awarded Dec 5, 2024; inference) [41]; Norway’s new emergency-network procurements with LEO as back-up [42,44]; SWEN air-to-ground and maritime coverage procurements [48]; the Dutch Kennemerland safety-region satcom tender [39]; Brazil’s SGDC-2 RFP and contract during 2027 [82]; and Korea’s possible new 2027 LEO budget line [62].
  • Portals: Section 1 lists 95 official portals. For civil satcom, TED (filter CPV 64227000, 64214100 and 32530000–32534000 and read the buyer name), Find a Tender, Doffin, Hilma, PhilGEPS, AusTender and Taiwan’s PCC system carried the live items found this month. Several portals block automated access (TED 202 bot check; Ofcom, INAPROC, DICT, ADB and FEMA return 403; GeM and NDMA failed TLS). They open normally in a browser, and each is flagged.

2. Europe: civil government satcom programmes and tenders

2.1 EU-level programmes and funding

Programme / buyer

Status (as of Nov 13, 2026)

Entry points

EU Critical Communication System (EUCCS) – DG HOME

PLANNED (legislative proposal). Proposed Sep 30, 2026; links national critical-comms systems in 31 EU and Schengen countries; national networks move to broadband, with EU satellites as back-up; Member States connect from 2030 [1]. Impact assessment cites €3.571bn of public investment; Art. 18 requires use of GOVSATCOM/IRIS² to extend or back up terrestrial networks, with service modes including stationary back-up, on-the-pause, on-the-move and direct-to-device [2].

After adoption by Parliament and Council: network and security monitoring centres, satellite-access integration, devices.

GOVSATCOM – EUSPA hub

OPERATING. Operational since January 2026; provides secure government satcom for authorised public users, including civil-security and crisis-management users [4]. Commission says commercial capabilities could be added from early 2027 and is negotiating Ukraine’s association [11].

Capacity providers offering into the pool; terminals and service integration for civil users.

IRIS² (civil/government services)

AWARDED. The Aug 7, 2026 agreement expands the constellation to 348 satellites, brings first launches forward to 2029, and adds 66 satellites for defence, security and emergency services [5]. BDBOS sees IRIS² as a key building block for German blue-light (BOS) communications [33].

User terminals and service integration for civil-security users; see the companion report for IRIS² supply-chain routes.

Digital Networks Act – DG CNECT

PLANNED (legislation). Proposal adopted Jan 21, 2026; introduces an EU-level satellite spectrum authorisation and cites the need to reduce dependence in satellite communications for crisis response [6].

Regulatory: pan-EU authorisation would ease multi-country civil satcom services.

BEREC Office – BEREC/2026/OP/0006

OPEN. Business-continuity and crisis-communication services and devices; total €186,860; Lot 1 satellite devices and services (max €159,160); tenders due Nov 19, 2026, 14:00 Riga time [7].

Satellite phone/terminal resellers.

Horizon Europe Cluster 3 – HORIZON-CL3-2026-01-DRS-03

CLOSED. Search-and-rescue tools and technologies (communications in scope); €8M; opened May 6, closed Nov 5, 2026 [8].

Next Cluster 3 work programme calls; consortium partner role for satcom firms.

ESA ARTES 4.0 4S – maritime safety and critical communications AO (ESA-CSC-T-AO-0003)

OPEN (rolling). Maritime safety and critical-communications demonstrations, implementation 2026–2028; open from November 2025 until at least November 2026; outline then full proposal [9].

Satcom operators and integrators with maritime/critical-comms demonstrators.

Iris (satellite ATM datalink) – ESA/ESSP

OPERATING. Four major ANSPs signed for commercial operations; Iris covers about 40% of European air traffic (Jun 1, 2026) [10].

Aviation safety; avionics and ANSP integration.

2.2 Blue-light and mission-critical networks

Network / buyer

Status and satellite role

Entry points

United Kingdom – ESN (Home Office ESMCP; EE/BT, IBM)

PENDING DELIVERY / RFI on satellite. ESN covers about 86% of Great Britain’s land mass (April 2026) vs about 82% for Airwave [21]. Full Voice Service Ready targeted March 2028, mass transition from Q4 2028, completion 18–21 months later; rapid-response vehicles already use LEO links [22]. UKSA ran a Sep 2025 expression-of-interest workshop on satellite augmentation [23], followed by a January 2026 D2D request for information [24]. Whole-life cost reported at £14bn [UNVERIFIED: press only] [25].

Satellite back-up and D2D gap-fill for remote areas; deployable LEO backhaul. Watch Find a Tender (UKSA/ESMCP).

France – Réseau Radio du Futur (RRF) (ACMOSS; Orange, Bouygues Telecom)

AWARDED / ROLL-OUT. National roll-out decided Sep 1, 2026; about 36,000 Préfecture de Police lines migrate Sep 2026–Feb 2027 [28]. Deployable base stations connect via satellite and deploy in 3 days in mainland France [29]; Rapid Response Solutions use a satellite link [30], via Eutelsat OneWeb for Bouygues [32]; vehicle relays tested on civil-security Starlink [31].

Sub-tier to Orange/Bouygues; vehicle relays and kits via ACMOSS/UGAP.

Germany – BOS digital radio / broadband (BDBOS)

PLANNED. BDBOS is studying satellite as a complement to next-generation BOS broadband, with IRIS² (operations from about 2030) seen as a main future building block [33,34]. Federal Pakt für den Bevölkerungsschutz: €10bn to 2029, including warning and communication systems [35]. Baden-Württemberg Interior Ministry awarded 90 Iridium PTT satellite radios [36].

Länder interior ministries, THW and BBK buys via service.bund.de/e-Vergabe; IRIS² user terminals later.

Netherlands – C2000 successor (VMX)

PLANNED. C2000 was to be replaced by mid-2027 at the latest under the NOOVA programme [38]; on Oct 22, 2026 the Bestuurlijk Meldkamer Beraad approved a first VMX development phase (controlled environment, up to 2,000 users), with its schedule due in early 2027 [37]. Safety regions are buying satellite back-up separately: Drenthe (3 dishes, €263,500, VEAT) [18]; Kennemerland market consultation closed Oct 28, 2026 ahead of a tender [39].

Safety-region satcom continuity tenders on TenderNed.

Sweden – SWEN / Rakel G2 (MCF, formerly MSB)

IN PROCUREMENT. Hybrid state/commercial architecture; Ericsson core delivered and in operation; final report to government Mar 1, 2027 [47]. PIN (Apr 14, 2026): RAN award expected Q2/Q3 2026; air-to-ground and maritime coverage may be procured separately [48]. RAN reportedly awarded to two MNOs on Sep 18, 2026 (SEK 2bn) [UNVERIFIED: press only] [49].

Air-to-ground and maritime coverage lots are the likeliest satellite entry points.

Norway – new Nødnett (DSB, Nkom)

PLANNED. To be based on national mobile networks; Nkom recommends multiple access technologies, with LEO satellites as back-up and for areas without mobile coverage (Oct 15, 2026) [42]. DSB ran an MCX RFI [44] and in 2023 received NOK 3M from the Norwegian Space Agency to trial LEO in today’s Nødnett [45]. Nkom is also piloting satellite-based back-up for mobile coverage in major incidents [43]. Space Norway signed a civil-preparedness MoU with Akkodis (Oct 22, 2026) [46].

Doffin; DSB procurements (timing not yet published).

Finland – Virve 2 (Erillisverkot)

OPERATING / MIGRATION. Broadband service live; migration from TETRA expected to run to end-2028 [50]. NESA highlights satellite broadband as back-up for network disruptions [51].

Hilma; satellite back-up via service partners.

AWARDED. Re-awarded to Telefónica for €328.18M incl. tax (Jul 30, 2026) [40]. No separate satcom lot was identified.

Sub-tier to Telefónica.

2.4 Ukraine

  • GOVSATCOM association: the EU Council authorised negotiations on Mar 9, 2026; the Commission said on Oct 14, 2026 that it is “in talks with Ukraine to fully associate Ukraine to Govsatcom” and that commercial capabilities could be added at the beginning of 2027 [11]. Status: PLANNED. Civil government users would reach satcom through the GOVSATCOM hub rather than national tenders; Prozorro carries Ukrainian national procurement.

How to use this watchlist

  • Set three automated searches now: (1) TED with CPV 64227000, 64214100 and 32530000–32534000, then discard defence buyers by name; (2) Find a Tender plus Contracts Finder for “satellite”, “ESMCP” and “resilience”; (3) PhilGEPS, AusTender and Taiwan PCC for “satellite”/“衛星”.
  • Expect satellite as a lot, not a programme: in blue-light procurements, look for air-to-ground, maritime, deployable and back-up lots (e.g., SWEN) [48], and for D2D gap-fill (UK ESN, Australia UOMO) [24,72].
  • Sovereignty is now a selection factor: France’s maritime-affairs award specified a sovereign LEO/GEO service [17], and Bouygues’ RRF kits use Eutelsat OneWeb backhaul [32]. Starlink-only frameworks still appear (Estonia) [12].

Caveats

  • This report covers non-military government buyers. Defence satcom (NCIA, EDA, SATCOMBw, SKYNET, national MoDs) is in the companion report; TED notices from armed-forces units were deliberately excluded.
  • No dedicated satellite procurement was found this month for ASTRID (Belgium), SIRDEE (Spain), Digital Bharat Nidhi (India), BAKTI LEO (Indonesia), Frontex, or Korea’s disaster-safety network; their portals are listed so new notices can be caught.
  • The UK ESN £14bn cost, Sweden’s SWEN RAN award, US BEAD satellite totals, nbn LEO timing, India’s subsidy rejection and the Korean K-LEO cost scenarios come from press or aggregators and are marked as such.
  • The EUCCS cost (€3.571bn) is the Commission’s impact-assessment estimate in a proposal not yet adopted by Parliament and Council.
  • PhilGEPS and DICT award results for PIALEOS were not visible this month; DICT’s procurement page returns 403 to automated requests.
  • “Inference” labels (Taiwan follow-on, Italy re-tender, Japan next DX call) are derived from official contract end dates or annual cycles, not announced plans.
